newsitem.title: UK: Thistle Hotels starts year strongly.
newsitem.headline: Thistle Hotels starts year strongly.

text.p: Thistle Hotels Plc said on Tuesday that its performance in the first two periods of 1997 was in line with expectations and "significantly" better than last year.
The newly-floated British hotels group, which is 46 percent owned by New Zealand's Brierley Investments Ltd, earlier announced that operating profit rose 19.5 percent in 1996 to 106.7 million pounds.
"Thistle has had a strong start to the year, with sales, volume and rate all growing most satisfactorily," chief executive Robert Peel said in a statement accompanying results.

Thistle was formerly known as the Mount Charlotte Group until it was taken over by Brierley in 1990. It was floated on the London stock exchange in October 1996, bringing Brierley's stake down from 70 percent.
The company made pre-tax profit before exceptionals of 60.1 million pounds in the year ending December 29, 1996, up 73 percent on the previous year.
Thistle had a pretax loss of 27.7 million after an exceptional charge of 87.8 million pounds made on the writedown of hotels and development sites.
Thistle said it planned to grow through internal expansion.
"There are significant opportunities to add shareholder value through re-investment and expansion of existing hotels without recourse to acquisition," said the firm.
The company said that the strength of sterling would affect volume from incoming markets, particularly Europe and Japan.
It will pay a final dividend 2.0 pence per share, as stated at the time of flotation.
By 0935 GMT, Thistle shares had lost 5-1/2 pence to stand at 200-1/2 pence.
